stem.en: Vikram says: "The cell wall is the outermost layer of a plant cell, so it must be the part that controls which substances enter." Which reply is correct?

text.en: He is right, because the wall lets in useful substances and blocks everything else that reaches it.

feedback.en: The wall is permeable to water and some dissolved minerals. It does not pick out what a cell needs.

text.en: He is wrong: the wall is permeable, and the membrane is selective.
He is right for large molecules only, and the membrane controls only the very small ones.

feedback.en: The wall does not control entry in this way. Selective permeability belongs to the membrane.

text.en: He is wrong, because plant cells do not take in any substances from the outside at all.

feedback.en: Plant root cells take in water and nutrients from the soil.

explanation.en: Being on the outside does not make the wall the controller. Water and some dissolved minerals pass through it, and the selectively permeable membrane just inside controls what enters the cell.

hints.en: Which layer is called selectively permeable?
